basis: Original source pixels only; the optional detail is a 3x source-only enlargement, not new geometry.

facts: One common pair of axes: a near-horizontal time axis with a right arrow and a near-vertical voltage axis with an up arrow.
The time axis extends left of the vertical axis and far right of the last trace endpoint. The voltage axis extends below the baseline and above both positive trace maxima.

An O is below-left of the intersection; t is below the right arrow. The voltage label is a u-like glyph with a small trailing/subscript-like glyph at the upper left; its precise modern transcription needs edition-text reconciliation, not a guessed source calibration.
There are no numbered ticks, units, explicit periods, calibration values, or extra axes.
A solid trace starts near (54, 277), rises approximately linearly through the baseline near (112, 175), and reaches a positive maximum near (173, 72).
A nearly vertical full reset at x approximately 172 drops from the first positive maximum to the negative floor near y 277.
The second rising run crosses the same baseline near (233, 177), reaches a comparable maximum near (295, 71), and resets fully near x 292 to y 278.
The third rising run crosses the baseline near (353, 179) and stops near (386, 128), below the previous positive maxima.
Totals: three rising runs, two full resets, three baseline crossings, two full positive maxima, and one incomplete final run. No fourth cycle or third reset is visible.
regularizationAllowed: Straighten scan tilt and stroke roughness; idealize the two completed runs as equally spaced without asserting a numerical time scale.
Preserve the final partial-run endpoint and all axis extensions instead of completing another cycle.

detail.method: sips -z 1473 1299; entire source enlarged 3x; no candidate or geometry input

facts: A tall dark outer casing contains a large round CRT screen, not a rectangular Cartesian plot.
The circular screen has a double rim. A light mounting plate remains visible at its four corner regions.
Four dark round fasteners appear one per corner region, approximately (85, 81), (354, 89), (74, 356), and (352, 357).
The screen is approximately centered at (215, 219), with radius about 164 pixels; the outer casing continues substantially below it.
No readable source caption, numeric calibration, coordinate labels, or arrowed axes are present.
The finite orthogonal lattice is visible only inside the circular screen; chords and limb fragments terminate at the screen boundary.
There are 19 vertical tracks, including the short left and right boundary tracks, and 17 horizontal tracks. These are tracks, not 19 by 17 cells.

Approximate vertical-track x centers on the source near mid/lower screen: 55, 74, 90, 109, 127, 145, 161, 179, 198, 214, 232, 251, 267, 283, 303, 319, 336, 355, 373. Scan skew changes x slightly along a track.

The shortest vertical tracks near x 55 and x 373 are visible near the side limbs. Top and bottom horizontal tracks near y 78 and y 365 are finite chords; the circular rim is not another horizontal grid track.

The lattice phase is offset relative to the circular screen: its central vertical track is near x 214 and central horizontal track near y 220; the horizontal-track family has less vertical extent than the vertical-track family.

An ideal finite carrier with 19 vertical and 17 horizontal tracks has 18 columns and 16 rows of intervals. Rendering a rectangular unmasked carrier, dropping boundary fragments, adding top/bottom tracks, or substituting an object count does not preserve this structure.
regularizationAllowed: Use equal spacing and remove scan skew while retaining track counts, distinct finite extents, phase relative to the circle, and clipped chord endpoints.
Exact ideal lattice coordinates are modern regularization, not numeric calibration read from the scan.

facts: One uninterrupted thick solid trace lies over the graticule and within the round screen.
At the left it starts around (72, 211), descends to a deep first trough around (85, 308), then rises to the largest visible positive peak around (129, 141).

It descends to a second trough around (160, 278), rises to a second positive peak around (199, 175), descends to a third trough around (230, 255), rises to a third peak around (266, 202), descends to a fourth shallow trough around (299, 239), and rises to a fourth small peak around (333, 215).
A final short descending tail ends around (353, 228); it does not become a flat horizontal line or grow a fifth peak/trough.
There are four visible troughs and four visible positive peaks, with decreasing excursions around an unlabelled central level. The first trough precedes the first positive peak.
No constant-amplitude sinusoid, dashed envelope, numerical voltage/time scale, added axes, labels naming the decay, or answer-bearing annotations occur in the source.
regularizationAllowed: Smooth jagged scan contours, retain the phase/order/count and relative source-graticule positions of every extremum and the terminal tail.
A regularized screen or smoother curve is not evidence for an exact physical calibration or an analytic decay law.
